playground.headline: E-paper handheld spins AI-generated choose-your-own adventures
playground.body: Jeremy Ngai built a handheld with a 2.9-inch e-paper screen, a rotary encoder, and an RGB LED for mood lighting. On first boot it connects to WiFi, then asks Gemini to generate a fresh choose-your-own-adventure story. The build uses a custom PCB and 3D-printed case, and runs about 20 hours per charge.
playground.why: It points to a future where portable reading gadgets generate endless interactive stories on demand.

playground.headline: Animated fortune teller Lillith dispenses servo-driven predictions
playground.body: Oh Well Why Not spent four months building Lillith, an animated fortune teller with servos and voice generation. Press the button and Lillith offers a glimpse of your future, with small servo animations while waiting for the next user. The build is documented as a roadmap for others to make their own.
playground.why: It shows how classic arcade fortune teller charm can be recreated with modern hobby servos and voice synthesis.

playground.headline: Offline voice-controlled brain for a simulated robot
playground.body: A solo developer built a Python brain for a Webots simulated environmental robot. You talk to it and it understands questions offline in Spanish, English, or Polish, then answers using simulated sensor data like temperature, humidity, air quality, and obstacles.
playground.why: It hints at robots that can understand spoken questions and report sensor readings without needing cloud services.

playground.headline: Engineer builds automated dog wash, dog remains unimpressed
playground.body: Stuff Made Here built an arch-like dog wash with oscillating spray nozzles, an air dryer, and an undercarriage nozzle running in a channel below the dog. The nozzles move on linear rails driven by a DC motor, with waterproofed electronics and AC power kept at a distance. The dog is terrified of the machine and won't use it, though the wash itself works.
playground.why: It shows that automated pet care is mechanically possible, even if the pets need some convincing.
